gloss: to be convinced; to be satisfied; to make sense

definitions.gloss: to be convinced; to be satisfied with an explanation; to make sense
definitions.explanation: To reach a state of understanding and acceptance about something. Often used when an explanation finally makes sense or when one is satisfied with the reasoning behind something.

examples.japanese: それなら{納得|なっとく}がいく。
{説明|せつめい}を{聞|き}いてやっと{納得|なっとく}がいった。
examples.english: After hearing the explanation, I was finally convinced.

examples.japanese: どうしても{納得|なっとく}がいかないので、もう{一度|いちど}{話|はな}し{合|あ}いたい。
examples.english: I'm just not satisfied with it, so I'd like to discuss it one more time.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}が{納得|なっとく}のいく{結果|けっか}が{出|で}るまで{続|つづ}ける。
examples.english: I'll keep going until I get a result I'm satisfied with.

notes:
A common expression combining {納得|なっとく} (acceptance, understanding) with the verb いく (to go). The negative form {納得|なっとく}がいかない (to not be satisfied, to not be able to accept) is used at least as frequently as the positive form. Can also appear as {納得|なっとく}のいく as a modifier before nouns.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {納得|なっとく}がいく: to be convinced / it makes sense
- {納得|なっとく}がいかない: to not be satisfied / it doesn't make sense
- {納得|なっとく}のいく + noun: a satisfactory ~
- {納得|なっとく}のいくまで: until one is satisfied

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {納得|なっとく}する: to be convinced — simpler construction with the same core meaning; {納得|なっとく}がいく emphasizes reaching the state of acceptance
- {合点|がてん}がいく: to understand, to be convinced — older/literary expression with a similar structure
- {腑|ふ}に{落|お}ちる: to make sense, to be persuaded — emphasizes the moment something clicks intuitively
